native_warning.evidence: Both archives show the same Key_Carrier floating-regions notice. Every R58-R65 slice had it, including the approved R63 pair. Each archive has its own layers.json: completely_unsupported_starts is [] for all 13 parts and native_support_moves is 0. Each verify.log shows blocked [] and unsupported_starts {}, and both receipts exited 0. The earlier 0.15 mm2 rear-socket fragment at layer 9 is gone. Each archive has six one-anchored runs. Two at layer 155 are identical to R63. Three at layers 10-11 sit at the same rear-socket stations as R63, but their lengths changed (1.05/1.02/2.16 here against R63's 1.55/2.58/1.90). The sixth is new: a straight 4.626 mm, 0.283 mm-wide outer-wall line at layer 49 (G-code line 131577). It starts at the free inboard end of the tapered outboard battery lip and runs to the wall: assembly X -18.98 to -23.60, Z ~3.04, Y ~33.95. It stops ~0.12 mm short of the outboard wall's inner face (-23.72). Evaluating taper_floor by hand gives only ~0.14 mm of lip at layer 48, below a bead width, so no plastic is expected under its free span. The leaf underside is at Z 3.74, ~0.56 mm above the line's top edge. The slicer does not say where its notice comes from. This line is the only new candidate; it is accepted as a monitored watch point, not as a reason for supports.
